title: Who Did the Governor-General Represent?
imageAlt: A simplified teaching guide for Who Did the Governor-General Represent?. It shows relationships and evidence questions, not an unchanged structure for every year or an original historical order.
content:
The governor-general was a leading official of the Spanish colonial government, acting under the authority of the Spanish Crown. The Crown means the monarchy and its authority, not only the object worn on a head. This office belonged to colonial government, not to a modern elected Philippine presidency.

An office and a person are different. Different people could hold the office at different times. Knowing one name does not explain all its responsibilities or establish that every holder acted identically. The arrangements of government also changed over the long colonial period.

Try a fictional museum-caption task. A caption calls the governor-general the elected president of an independent Philippine republic. Correct the relationship: this was an official of an outside colonial monarchy. Do not replace one misleading title with a claim that the official could act without laws or other institutions.

Our diagram is a simplified relationship guide, not a complete chart for every year.
clues: The Crown
The Spanish monarchy was the source of colonial authority represented by the office.
Office and holder
An office can have different holders. One person's actions do not describe every period.
Avoid a modern substitution
A colonial governor-general was not the elected president of a modern independent Philippine republic.
task: Which label fits the office in this mission?
A leading colonial official acting under the Spanish Crown
The elected president of a modern independent Philippine republic
A leader chosen identically by every local community
A person without any relationship to the monarchy
reason: The office represented Spanish colonial authority. Distinguish it from a modern presidency and from any one officeholder.

title: Responsibilities Were More Than a Title
imageAlt: A simplified teaching guide for Responsibilities Were More Than a Title. It shows relationships and evidence questions, not an unchanged structure for every year or an original historical order.
content:
Central government involved administration, resources and defense. The governor-general held broad responsibilities, including the military role associated with captain-general. Broad responsibilities did not mean one person personally carried out every task. Officials, navigators, messengers and local participants all mattered.

A responsibility tells what an office was meant to do. It does not prove how well a duty was performed. To investigate performance, ask what decisions were made, who acted and what consequences followed.

Watch how to sort a fictional record. A description of an office's defense duty names a responsibility. A later report about supplies reaching a particular place concerns an action and its result. Keep those categories separate before evaluating the official.

The examples are classroom exercises, not recovered orders. Later missions examine local offices and particular systems; this scene introduces central responsibilities without claiming that one chart describes every year or that all communities experienced government identically.
clues: Administration
Central officials made and coordinated governing decisions; many people were needed to carry them out.
Defense
The office had military responsibilities associated with captain-general, alongside civil responsibilities.
Duty versus performance
A responsibility does not establish that it was fulfilled fairly or effectively. Check actions and consequences.
task: Which explanation treats responsibilities carefully?
The office had civil and military responsibilities carried out through many participants
One official performed every task alone
A duty proves it was always performed fairly
A title reveals every resident's approval
reason: Broad duties involved administration and defense. Their actual performance requires evidence, not assumptions based on title.
definition: A duty an office or person is expected to carry out.

title: How Did a Central Decision Reach People?
imageAlt: A simplified teaching guide for How Did a Central Decision Reach People?. It shows relationships and evidence questions, not an unchanged structure for every year or an original historical order.
content:
A central decision did not travel by itself. Written messages, officials and resources connected a governing center with particular places. An order's issue, delivery and implementation are separate events. Implementation means putting a decision into practice.

Your earlier investigations showed why a colonial base did not establish immediate control everywhere. The same question applies here: where and when was a decision carried out, and how did people respond? A central-government chart describes relationships; it is not evidence that every arrow worked perfectly.

Try a fictional worked example. A record shows an order was issued in Manila. A second record shows that a messenger delivered it elsewhere. Neither alone tells whether it was put into practice there. Seek evidence of the later action and local responses.

Do not invent a universal response or treat distance as the only factor. Resources, relationships, knowledge and resistance could shape what happened. Local government and Indigenous leadership are the next mission's focus.
clues: Issue
An order being issued establishes a decision, not all later actions.
Delivery
Evidence of delivery differs from evidence that a decision was put into practice.
Implementation
Check actions in the affected place, together with local responses and limits.
task: An order was issued and delivered. What still needs checking?
Whether and how it was put into practice in the affected place
Nothing, because delivery proves universal obedience
Only the official's title written again
Every resident's thoughts can now be assumed
reason: Issue, delivery and implementation are separate. Investigate what happened in particular places rather than assuming every decision worked.
definition: Putting a decision or plan into practice.

title: Another Institution: The Audiencia
imageAlt: A simplified teaching guide for Another Institution: The Audiencia. It shows relationships and evidence questions, not an unchanged structure for every year or an original historical order.
content:
The Real Audiencia de Manila was an institution with judicial and other governmental functions. Judicial means connected with courts and judging legal matters. The Supreme Court's historical account describes it as a court with additional executive, advisory and administrative roles.

The governor-general also served as its presiding officer in the historical arrangement described by that account. Do not imagine two entirely unrelated boxes that never shared responsibilities. At the same time, a court and a governor's office are different concepts, and neither is the whole of government.

For this fictional exhibit task, compare a caption saying the governor was the only institution with a source naming the Audiencia. Correct the caption while keeping a limit: the existence of an institution does not prove that all decisions were fair or that every person had equal access to justice.

This is an introductory overview. Institutional powers and arrangements changed; our simple guide is not a modern separation-of-powers chart or an unchanged structure for every colonial year.
clues: Judicial work
The Audiencia handled court matters and had additional governmental functions in the historical account.
Overlapping roles
The governor-general could preside over the Audiencia. Responsibilities were not identical to a modern government chart.
A limit on conclusions
An institution's existence does not prove universal fairness, access or effective enforcement.
task: Which caption uses the Audiencia evidence carefully?
It was a court with other governmental roles; its existence does not prove universal fairness
The governor was the only institution that existed
The Audiencia was identical to every modern government branch
Having a court guarantees every person equal access
reason: The Audiencia had judicial and other roles, including institutional overlap. Its existence alone does not establish fair outcomes for everyone.
definition: Connected with courts and judging legal matters.

title: An Order Is Not Everyone's Experience
imageAlt: A simplified teaching guide for An Order Is Not Everyone's Experience. It shows relationships and evidence questions, not an unchanged structure for every year or an original historical order.
content:
A record can tell us what an official ordered without telling us every effect. It may emphasize a duty, an intended result or the official's own explanation. Local accounts and evidence of actions can help test the claim.

The Library of Congress discussion of colonial relationships highlights local interests and connections. This helps us ask who participated and whose viewpoint is missing from a simple account of central power. It does not mean all official records are useless; it means their claims need careful reading.

Work through a fictional report: the governor ordered supplies moved, so every household benefited equally. The first clause describes an order. The second needs separate evidence about delivery, implementation and effects on people. A good report states the gap rather than fills it with an invented speech.

Ask what the record establishes and what remains uncertain. The office's broad power did not make every resident's experience identical, and criticism of a particular action does not make all people in a group the same.
clues: Identify the record
An official account may describe an order or intention rather than the complete result.
Check consequences
Evidence about implementation and affected people is needed for claims about benefits or harms.
Respect the limit
One source does not reveal every person's thoughts or prove identical experiences.
task: A report says an order benefited everyone equally, but gives no outcome evidence. What should a learner do?
Separate the recorded order from the unproven claim about effects
Accept the effect because an official issued the order
Invent household statements to make the claim convincing
Treat the official's intention as every person's experience
reason: A recorded order needs separate evidence of implementation and effects. Keep source viewpoint and uncertainty visible.
definition: What the available evidence cannot establish by itself.

title: Build Your Central Government Report
imageAlt: A report guide distinguishes colonial authority, responsibilities and institutions from evidence of implementation and effects. The chapter is still partial.
content: Explain central government without turning it into one person doing everything. Identify the governor-general's relationship to the Spanish Crown. Connect a responsibility with the people and resources needed to carry it out. Distinguish an issued decision, its delivery and its implementation. Include the Audiencia as another institution with judicial and other roles. Do not force the arrangement into a modern government chart or assume the existence of a court proves fairness for all. Keep period, place and the limits of the source in your explanation. Use this fictional report frame in your own words: The office represented [authority]. Its responsibilities included [duty]. The evidence records [action], but we need [further evidence] to assess its effects on [affected people]. This is a classroom guide, not an original speech. The five-question quiz checks these ideas. Revisit difficult topics and use targeted practice before retrying. Passing earns the mission reward once. Complete all missions, then pass the chapter challenge to earn the chapter badge.
clues: Explain the office
Distinguish the Crown, an office and its different holders.
Explain the process
Connect duties and institutions with issue, delivery and implementation.
Explain the evidence
Ask whose account survives and what further evidence is needed for effects on people.
task: Which final explanation fits the investigation?
Central offices represented colonial authority, while implementation and effects required many participants and further evidence
One official acted alone and all decisions worked identically everywhere
A court's existence proves universal fairness
A delivered order reveals every household's private thoughts
reason: Explain colonial offices and responsibilities while distinguishing institutional relationships from evidence of actual effects.
definition: Institutions responsible for governing decisions from a central level.
